newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: No South African cabinet reshuffle - Mandela.
newsitem.headline: No South African cabinet reshuffle - Mandela.

text.p: South Africa's President Nelson Mandela said on Friday he had no plans for an imminent cabinet reshuffle.

In off the cuff remarks during his opening of parliament address Mandela joked that he has spotted some cabinet ministers "dozing" while he was speaking. He said he thought he ought to drop them, but then looked around and saw that provincial premiers and members of opposition were also dozing.
To loud laughter Mandela then said: "I thought I should be fair and not be discriminatory, so there will be no reshuffle for the time being."
Earlier this year there were rumours of a reshuffle, including the possibility of shifting Finance Minister Trevor Manuel to foreign affairs. Manuel denied the reports at the time.
